title: PP-PicoDet: A Better Real-Time Object Detector on Mobile Devices
key_idea: Family of anchor-free lightweight detectors with an improved backbone, a light neck, better label assignment and loss, tuned for mobile CPUs; positioned against YOLOX-Nano and NanoDet.
method: Architecture and training optimizations for small anchor-free detectors; latency measured on mobile ARM CPUs.
data: Mobile ARM CPU at input size 320 (benchmark dataset not named in the abstract)
reported_result: Abstract: PicoDet-S has 0.99M parameters and 30.6% mAP, 4.8 points above YOLOX-Nano with 55% lower mobile CPU latency, and runs at 123 FPS (150 FPS with Paddle Lite) on a mobile ARM CPU at input 320; PicoDet-L has 3.3M parameters and 40.9% mAP.
relation_to_project: Slides 01-05, frozen detector element: a small-detector alternative to YOLOX-Nano with published CPU timings; input to the latency budget of card X3-3.
code_or_data: https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleDetection (named in the arXiv abstract; not opened; licence not read)
notes: Preprint, not peer reviewed. Hub (read-only): the PicoDet models found are PaddlePaddle layout-analysis variants with apache-2.0 tags, not general detectors; the Hub paper page links no model. Timings are for a mobile ARM CPU, not a laptop.

title: EfficientDet: Scalable and Efficient Object Detection
venue: 2020 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
key_idea: Detector family built from a weighted bidirectional feature pyramid (BiFPN) and compound scaling of resolution, depth and width, giving a size ladder across resource limits with official code.
method: BiFPN multi-scale feature fusion plus uniform compound scaling of backbone, feature network and box and class heads.
reported_result: Abstract: the largest model, EfficientDet-D7, reaches 55.1 AP on COCO test-dev with 77M parameters and 410B FLOPs, 4x to 9x smaller and using 13x to 42x fewer FLOPs than earlier detectors; no timing of the small models in the abstract.
relation_to_project: Card X3-1: candidate architecture for a second detector in a detector-disagreement cue; only the small end of the family is a laptop candidate and needs a timing test.
code_or_data: https://github.com/google/automl/tree/master/efficientdet (named in the arXiv abstract; not opened; licence not read)
notes: Abstract read from the arXiv record 1911.09070 (2019); the DOI is the CVPR 2020 version. No laptop timing read.

title: MobileNetV2: Inverted Residuals and Linear Bottlenecks
venue: 2018 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
key_idea: Mobile backbone of inverted residual blocks with linear bottlenecks; the paper also defines SSDLite, a light detection framework, and a reduced DeepLabv3 for mobile segmentation.
method: Depthwise-convolution backbone with thin bottleneck layers, used with SSDLite for detection.
data: ImageNet classification, COCO detection, VOC segmentation (abstract)
relation_to_project: Slides 01-05, frozen detector and crop-classifier elements: SSDLite is a light detector option; MobileNetV2 is the reference that MobileNetV3 (P2-P2425, DECK_SRC) improves on.
code_or_data: No code location stated in the abstract read
notes: Abstract read from the arXiv record 1801.04381; the abstract gives no numbers. Hub (read-only): jack-perlo/MobileNetV2-Gtsrb, a keras GTSRB classifier without a licence tag, community upload, UNVERIFIED.

title: ShuffleNet V2: Practical Guidelines for Efficient CNN Architecture Design
key_idea: Argues that FLOPs are an indirect proxy and that speed must be measured on the target platform, derives practical design guidelines from controlled experiments, and proposes the ShuffleNet V2 backbone.
method: Controlled speed experiments on target hardware, design guidelines including memory access cost, and a new efficient backbone.
reported_result: Abstract: ablation experiments support a leading speed and accuracy trade-off; no number in the abstract.
relation_to_project: Owner contribution 5 and card X3-3: supports timing the whole pipeline on the owner's laptop instead of quoting FLOPs; candidate small backbone for a crop classifier.
code_or_data: No code location stated in the abstract read
notes: Crossref lists only the book series; the conference name was not in the record read. Abstract read from the arXiv record 1807.11164.

title: DETRs Beat YOLOs on Real-time Object Detection
venue: 2024 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
key_idea: Real-time end-to-end transformer detector (RT-DETR) without NMS, using an efficient hybrid encoder and uncertainty-minimal query selection; speed can be tuned by the number of decoder layers without retraining.
method: Hybrid encoder that decouples intra-scale interaction and cross-scale fusion, query selection, adjustable decoder depth.
reported_result: Abstract: RT-DETR-R50 and R101 reach 53.1% and 54.3% AP on COCO at 108 and 74 FPS on a T4 GPU, and 55.3% and 56.2% AP after Objects365 pre-training.
relation_to_project: Card X3-1: a transformer detector as the second, architecturally different model for a detector-disagreement cue; R18 weights on the Hub run in HF transformers.
code_or_data: Project page https://zhao-yian.github.io/RTDETR (named in the arXiv abstract); the Hub card PekingU/rtdetr_r18vd names https://github.com/lyuwenyu/RT-DETR and carries an apache-2.0 tag (uploader statement); not opened
notes: Abstract read from the arXiv record 2304.08069 (2023). Hub (read-only): PekingU/rtdetr_r18vd 21.0K and rtdetr_v2_r18vd 175.1K downloads listed, apache-2.0 tags. Timings are for a T4 GPU, not a laptop.

title: MMDetection: Open MMLab Detection Toolbox and Benchmark
key_idea: Open detection toolbox with training and inference code for many detection and instance-segmentation methods, weights for more than 200 models, and a benchmarking study of methods and hyper-parameters.
method: Unified modular codebase and model zoo; benchmark of methods, components and hyper-parameters.
reported_result: Abstract: provides weights for more than 200 network models; no accuracy number in the abstract.
relation_to_project: Cards X3-1 and X3-2: one codebase that supplies several frozen detectors for transfer and disagreement tests; SAHI (P2-P2423, DECK_SRC) states integration with it.
code_or_data: https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection (named in the arXiv abstract; not opened; licence not read)

title: Simple online and realtime tracking
venue: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP)
key_idea: Online multi-object tracker that links detections frame to frame with only a Kalman filter and the Hungarian algorithm; shows that tracking quality depends mainly on detection quality.
method: Kalman-filter motion model plus Hungarian assignment of detector boxes.
reported_result: Abstract: changing the detector changes tracking performance by up to 18.9%; the tracker updates at 260 Hz, over 20 times faster than other trackers compared.
relation_to_project: Slide 05, tracker element: a near-free tracker for track-level consistency (a box that vanishes inside a live track); its dependence on detection quality is also what an attack exploits.
code_or_data: No code location stated in the abstract read
notes: Abstract read from the arXiv record 1602.00763.

title: ByteTrack: Multi-object Tracking by Associating Every Detection Box
key_idea: Associates almost every detection box, including low-score ones, with existing tracklets to recover occluded objects and drop background boxes; works as a generic add-on to many trackers.
method: Two-stage association: high-score boxes first, then low-score boxes matched to tracklets by similarity.
reported_result: Abstract: 80.3 MOTA, 77.3 IDF1 and 63.1 HOTA on the MOT17 test set at 30 FPS on one V100 GPU; IDF1 gains of 1 to 10 points when the association is added to 9 trackers.
relation_to_project: Slide 05 and owner contribution 2: low-score boxes kept by the tracker are candidate evidence of objects whose confidence an attack suppressed (hypothesis to test); reports BDD100K tracking.
code_or_data: https://github.com/ifzhang/ByteTrack (named in the arXiv abstract with deploy versions; not opened; licence not read)
notes: Crossref lists only the book series; abstract read from the arXiv record 2110.06864 (2021). Timing is for a V100 GPU, not a laptop.

title: Fast Optical Flow Using Dense Inverse Search
key_idea: Dense optical flow at very low cost: inverse search for patch correspondences, patch aggregation across scales into a dense field, then variational refinement; built for time-critical uses such as tracking.
method: Inverse compositional patch search, multi-scale densification, variational refinement.
reported_result: Abstract: runs at 300 Hz up to 600 Hz on a single CPU core, with accuracy competitive on large-displacement optical-flow benchmarks.
relation_to_project: Slide 05 independent cue (optical flow) and slide 02 camera-motion correction: a CPU-only flow cue that fits the laptop budget.
code_or_data: No code location stated in the abstract read
notes: Crossref lists only the book series; abstract read from the arXiv record 1603.03590. Timing as stated by the authors, not a laptop measurement.

title: T-SEA: Transfer-Based Self-Ensemble Attack on Object Detection
venue: 2023 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
key_idea: Single-model transfer attack: an adversarial patch optimised on one detector, with self-ensembling over input data, the attacked model and the patch, transfers to several black-box detectors.
method: Adjusted patch-training strategy plus self-ensemble on data, model and patch; combinable with PGD and MIM.
reported_result: Abstract: greatly improves black-box transferability of the patch across mainstream detectors and also raises white-box performance; no number in the abstract.
relation_to_project: Threatens card X3-1 and any disagreement cue between two detectors: one patch may fool several detectors at once; its code is a ready generator of transfer attacks for the evaluation.
code_or_data: https://github.com/VDIGPKU/T-SEA (named in the arXiv abstract; not opened; licence not read)
notes: Abstract read from the arXiv record 2211.09773 (2022). The LIT_A5 row P2-P527 names T-SEA in its own text.

title: DPatch: An Adversarial Patch Attack on Object Detectors
key_idea: Patch attack that targets both box regression and classification of detectors such as Faster R-CNN and YOLO; small, location-independent, untargeted or targeted, and transferable across detectors.
method: Optimise a small patch against detector regression and classification; black-box transfer evaluation.
reported_result: Abstract: lowers the mAP of Faster R-CNN from 75.10% and of YOLO from 65.7% to below 1%; a patch trained on one of the two detectors attacks the other.
relation_to_project: Slide 01 attack set: an early digital patch attack on detectors, cheap to run in an evaluation; digital, not physical.
code_or_data: No code location stated in the abstract read
notes: Preprint, not peer reviewed; a published version was not checked. Dataset behind the mAP values not named in the abstract.

title: Adversarial Robustness Toolbox v1.0.0
key_idea: Python library of adversarial attacks and defences across many model types and frameworks, covering input pre-processing, adversarial training, certification and runtime detection of modified inputs.
method: Framework-agnostic implementations of attacks, defences and detectors, with notebooks and documentation.
relation_to_project: Cards X3-1 and X3-2: a licensed source of attacks and runtime-detection baselines for the frozen-detector pipeline; whether its detector attacks fit YOLOX or RT-DETR is still to be checked.
code_or_data: https://github.com/IBM/adversarial-robustness-toolbox, MIT licence (both stated in the arXiv abstract of release 1.0.0; repository not opened; the current location and licence may differ)
notes: Preprint, not peer reviewed (white paper of release 1.0.0). Hub searches for the toolbox found no model or Space.

title: Torchattacks: A PyTorch Repository for Adversarial Attacks
key_idea: PyTorch library of adversarial attacks for generating adversarial examples and checking model robustness.
method: Library of attack implementations for PyTorch models.
relation_to_project: Card X3-2: quick digital attacks on a PyTorch sign classifier or crop classifier (the independent cue) to stress the consistency check; the abstract does not mention detectors.
code_or_data: https://github.com/Harry24k/adversarial-attacks-pytorch (named in the arXiv abstract; not opened; licence not read)

title: Foolbox Native: Fast adversarial attacks to benchmark the robustness of machine learning models in PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX
key_idea: Library of fast adversarial attacks for benchmarking model robustness, running natively in PyTorch, TensorFlow and JAX (from the title; abstract not read).
relation_to_project: Card X3-2: alternative attack library for the classifier side of the pipeline.
notes: Journal article per the Crossref record; the record carried no abstract.

category: X3-F2 Official code of defenses and detectors
title: Feature Squeezing: Detecting Adversarial Examples in Deep Neural Networks
venue: Proceedings 2018 Network and Distributed System Security Symposium
key_idea: Training-free detector: compare the model prediction on the original input with predictions on squeezed versions (reduced colour bit depth, spatial smoothing); a large disagreement flags an adversarial input.
method: Prediction-consistency test under cheap input transformations, with joint detection over several squeezers.
reported_result: Abstract: detects adversarial examples with high accuracy and few false positives; the two squeezers are inexpensive and complementary; no number in the abstract.
relation_to_project: All five slides, consistency check element: the simplest training-free consistency baseline, which a cue-based check should beat at matched false alarms; built for digital perturbations on classifiers, not physical attacks on detectors.
code_or_data: No code location stated in the abstract read
notes: Abstract read from the arXiv record 1704.01155 (2017). Rows P2-P211 (LIT_A2), P2-P509 (LIT_A5) and P2-P2103 (LIT_X12) name feature squeezing in their text.

category: X3-F2 Official code of defenses and detectors
title: Local Gradients Smoothing: Defense Against Localized Adversarial Attacks
venue: 2019 IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
key_idea: Training-free patch defense: locate localized adversarial noise from concentrated high-frequency gradients and suppress those regions before inference, with little effect on the salient object.
method: Gradient-domain localization of patch noise and regularization of image gradients in that region.
reported_result: Abstract: compared with watermarking, JPEG compression, total variance minimization and feature squeezing on ImageNet, it is the most resistant to the BPDA adaptive attack in the localized setting; no number in the abstract.
relation_to_project: Slide 01: a cheap image-domain cue for patch regions (high-frequency concentration) and a baseline; classifier setting, not detectors or physical signs.
code_or_data: No code location stated in the abstract read
notes: Abstract read from the arXiv record 1807.01216 (2018).
